text: Rian clearly had some different directions to take the whole thing, which would have been ace. The problem was Abrams went first in this weird experiment of "you write the first line" and did the right thing - set the opening scene, bridged the gap between the old films and shuffled things forward, created the conflict points, lay some open mysteries for later resolution. Sure it was a bit formulaic, but it was a strong foundation. Rian then decided to then use the second act to say "lol none of that shit matters. Snoke was just a guy, he's dead now. Rey doesn't have any connection to anything. Phasma just dies in a fight. Those potential love stories? Fuck 'em. Poe's neutered now, and Flynn is off on a pointless sidequest... THAT'S THE MIDDLE, NOW OVER TO YOU!" It's little fucking wonder Abrams struggled to stick the landing. I don't know if it was the wisest decision for him to go "uh, I dunno what that was about, but anyway back to the story I was trying to tell" and maybe he should have carried on going off the rails, but it fucking baffles me that nobody thought to sit down and map a billion dollar franchise out first with some rough notes. ESPECIALLY a franchise that was infamous for having a disjointed, badly written trilogy before it.
